title: One Honest Party Randomness Demo
description: Commit-reveal joint randomness over caller-supplied or crypto.getRandomValues contributions. Each of 3 to 7 parties publishes SHA-256(contribution concatenated with ceremony salt) before any reveal, then reveals; the ceremony output is SHA-256 over the ordered reveals. An all-but-one-dishonest toggle shows the output stays unpredictable while a single contribution is fresh. Paste mode lets two real devices exchange commitments then reveals by copy and paste with no network. An honesty panel demonstrates the last-revealer abort attack in-page and names the mitigations real protocols add. Teaching model, not a randomness beacon.

salt.description: Ceremony salt string mixed into every commitment.

partyCount.description: Number of simulated parties, integer in [3, 7].

contributions.description: Per-party contribution strings; empty entries are filled with crypto.getRandomValues entropy.

dishonestMode.description: When true, all parties except party 1 reuse a stale committed contribution instead of fresh entropy.

mcp_tool_definition.name: demo_commit_reveal_randomness
mcp_tool_definition.description: Runs a commit-reveal joint randomness ceremony over declared contributions and a declared salt: per-party commitments first, then reveals, with SHA-256 over the ordered reveals as the output. Returns the commitment list, the output hash, and a full transcript. Teaching demonstration, not a randomness beacon.
